heading: Mutual Fund Tax: How Portfolio Mix Changes Your Capital Gains Bill
tldr: The capital gains tax on your mutual fund investments depends on the fund's underlying portfolio, not just its category.
Funds holding over 65% in Indian equities are treated as equity-oriented for tax purposes.
Funds holding less than 65% in Indian equities are considered non-equity oriented for tax, regardless of their category.
This classification dictates the applicable holding period (12 or 36 months) for long-term capital gains and the tax rates.
Always check the fund's portfolio disclosure or factsheet to confirm its tax classification before investing or redeeming.
caption:
Did you know how your mutual funds are taxed isn't always straightforward? It actually depends on what the fund invests in, not just its name! Funds investing mostly in Indian shares get one tax treatment, while others get a different one. This matters for how long you need to hold them and how much tax you pay.
